short: The first major deployment of poison gas on the Western Front, which created a deep breach in the Allied lines around Ypres.
full:
On 22 April 1915, following a heavy artillery bombardment, German forces released 168 tons of chlorine gas across a four-mile front near Ypres. The dense yellow-green cloud drifted into the trenches held by French colonial troops, causing mass panic and suffocation. The untested weapon completely shattered the defensive line, opening a massive gap that the German infantry was initially unprepared to fully exploit.

Canadian and British units rushed forward to seal the breach, fighting desperately over the next month in an environment contaminated by lingering gas. Although the Allies ultimately prevented a total collapse of the salient, they suffered nearly 70,000 casualties and were forced to relinquish significant high ground. The introduction of chemical weapons fundamentally altered the psychological and tactical reality of the war, prompting an immediate race to develop both effective respirators and retaliatory gases.
